design.title: Cross-survey style mixing inside the borrowed eyes: during training, the early trunk layers' per-channel feature statistics (the 'look' of a photograph) are randomly blended with another view's from a different survey, so the place description cannot key on any one survey's style
design.init_strategy: pretrained:mobilenet_v3_small IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..10] (torchvision, BSD-3), fine-tuned at 0.1x LR (unchanged from experiment 13)
design.eli5: Each of the three aerial surveys of Berlin has its own 'look': one is a lush summer, one bare winter trees, one early spring, each processed by a different camera and lab. The model's early layers notice that look as overall averages, a bit like a photo filter. While training, we now randomly swap a blend of another survey's filter onto each picture inside the model, keeping the streets and rooftops exactly where they are. The model sees every street in many in-between styles, so a fourth survey with a style it has never seen looks like more of the same, and it has to recognise the place itself.
design.hypothesis: Builds on experiments 12-13 (pretrained trunk, kept) and experiment 4 (pixel-level nuisance randomisation, kept), and is the feature-level successor to experiment 6 (pixel blending of surveys, reverted). Experiments 12->13 moved held-out truedop_2024 usable from 10.75% to 49.5% to 60.25% (false fix 7.0 -> 5.5 -> 3.75%) purely by giving the place feature more of the ImageNet trunk's invariance: the stage that decides what a place looks like is where transfer to a new survey is won. But the trunk still encodes survey: exp 13's clean survey diagnostic on TRAINING positions ends at xs_cos_same 0.657, within-place variance fraction 0.235 and cross-survey argmax agreement only ~0.74 between the three training photographs, while the training photographs themselves score 0.013-0.038 (97-99% usable) and the held-out one 0.435 with 36% abstention. So a quarter of the embedding's variance is still 'which survey', and on a fourth survey that shifts the embedding off its tile prototype, which the committee min-mass gate turns into an abstention (coverage 64%, but 94% of answered frames correct). The answer is not more decode gating; it is a trunk whose mid-level features carry less survey style. Pixel-level augmentation (exp 4) can only perturb global exposure/colour/blur; the survey differences that remain (season, canopy, shadow length, texture rendering, sharpening/compression of each orthophoto pipeline) live in the per-channel mean and std of early CNN feature maps, which is exactly what style-transfer work identifies as 'style' (AdaIN). MixStyle (Zhou et al., ICLR 2021) regularises a pretrained CNN against unseen domains by replacing, at random during training, each instance's early-layer channel statistics with a convex mix of its own and another instance's. Our batches are survey-mixed by construction (paired-position interleave), so the partner is a different survey's photograph about two-thirds of the time: every place is shown wearing styles interpolated between the three surveys, which is the continuum experiment 6 tried to create in pixel space but with the content (spatial layout of the feature map) left intact rather than ghosted. A fourth survey's style is far more likely to fall inside that continuum than on one of three points.
